extracted.intended_audience: mathematics students, educators, and general readers interested in mathematics pedagogy
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes characteristics, abilities, and stage-progression that constitute 'mathematical maturity' and how students typically develop from computation-focused beginners to post-rigorous, research-ready practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: mastery of mathematicians' thinking/communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical maturity refers to the mastery of the way mathematicians think, operate and communicate; a mixture of mathematical experience and insight that cannot be directly taught.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a gauge of students' erudition in mathematical structures and methods; develops from repeated exposure rather than direct instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fearlessness in the face of symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to read and understand notation, to introduce clear and useful notation when appropriate (and not otherwise), and a general facility of expression in the terse—but crisp and exact—language mathematicians use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know when to introduce notation and when to avoid unnecessary symbolism; communicate concisely and precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to generalize
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to generalize from a specific example to a broad concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move from particular instances to formulating broader statements or conjectures; use examples as stepping stones to abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to handle increasingly abstract ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Comfort with and competence at working with abstract mathematical concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progressively accept abstraction (e.g., abstract algebraic structures, general topological notions) and manipulate them reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to communicate mathematically (notation and style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning standard notation and acceptable mathematical style to express ideas clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conventional notation and accepted stylistic norms so others can read and critique your work; clarity is part of maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift from memorization to understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant shift from learning by memorization to learning through understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize comprehension of concepts and proofs over memorizing procedures or results; use understanding to reconstruct or adapt facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to separate key ideas from less significant details
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to identify the central ideas (the crux) of an argument and distinguish them from peripheral technicalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winnow the chaff from the wheat; focus on the intent and driving insights of a proof or problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link geometric and analytic representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to link a geometrical representation with an analytic representation (and vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate between diagrammatic intuition and formal algebraic/analytic expressions; use both to check and inform arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate verbal problems into mathematical ones
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to convert informal or verbal descriptions of problems into precise mathematical statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify assumptions, variables, and appropriate formalisms when modeling real-world or word problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize valid proofs and detect sloppy thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to recognize a valid proof and to detect 'sloppy' or invalid reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discern sound argumentation from errors; learn to produce rigorous proofs and to critique others'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern recognition in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to recognize mathematical patterns, themes, currents and eddies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot recurring structures, analogies, and motifs across problems and fields to guide conjecture and solution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move between geometric (graph) and analytical (equation) viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Facility in moving back and forth between graphical/visual and algebraic/analytic descriptions of mathematical objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use each perspective as a sanity check and to gain complementary insights into a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop improved intuition by abandoning naive assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving mathematical intuition by abandoning naive assumptions and developing a more critical attitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine instincts through exposure to counterexamples and formalism; avoid clinging to misleading heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make and use connections across problems and disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The habit of connecting a given problem to other problems, results, or even other disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage cross-connections to import techniques and insights; interdisciplinary thinking is a maturity marker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to fill in missing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill at supplying omitted steps or justifications in arguments or proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comfortably reconstruct intermediate steps and verify hidden assumptions; this supports reading and producing concise proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot, correct, and learn from mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize errors, correct them, and extract lessons to avoid repeating them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mistakes as learning opportunities; maintain practices (sanity checks, simple tests) that catch errors early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and appreciate elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: An aesthetic sense for elegant, insightful solutions or proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value simplicity and conceptual clarity; seek proofs that illuminate rather than merely verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think abstractly
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity for abstract thought—reasoning about structures and relations rather than concrete computations alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate and manipulate abstract definitions and proofs; prefer structural understanding where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read, write, and critique formal proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Competence in composing formal proofs and critically reading others' proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Master proof techniques and standards of rigor; critique should detect gaps and evaluate correctness and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate knowns from unknowns
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to draw a line between what is known and what remains to be shown or assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify assumptions and the target claim; plan proof strategies based on this distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply knowledge creatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Use existing knowledge and techniques in novel or creative ways to solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine tools from different areas or adapt known methods to new contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The skill of making appropriate approximations when exact solutions are intractable or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand error bounds and when approximations preserve needed properties of a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-directed learning (teach oneself)
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to learn new material independently without relying on step-by-step instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop strategies to read textbooks/papers, fill gaps, and progress through topics autonomously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained attention and perseverance on challenging mathematical tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain concentration to follow long arguments and to work through subtle technical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring instinct and intuition to bear judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Use intuition and instinct where helpful, but check them against formality and rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance heuristics with formal verification; heuristics should suggest routes, not replace proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage: Pre-rigorous (beginner) characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to learning mathematical formalism: informal learning, reliance on examples, fuzzy notions and hand-waving; intuition-dominated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common features include natural talent importance and formal errors from blind application of heuristics; these errors may be hard to correct and require exposure to formalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage: Rigorous (intermediate) characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Onset of formal logic and proof techniques (transition/intro to proofs/discrete math/analysis); emphasis on theory and comfortable manipulation of abstract objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are exposed to counterexamples and learn to discern sound argumentation; risks include getting stalled by discarding too much intuition and susceptibility to formal errors that persist without sanity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage: Post-rigorous (advanced) characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Return to a more intuitive mindset informed by refined intuition and formal training; intuition and formalism are interwoven to sketch arguments and later formalize them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stage optimizes problem-solving efficiency and readies students for reading research papers; beware imprecise translation when formalism is suspended for expedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical advice (Terry Tao's guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: After becoming comfortable with rigorous mathematical thinking, revisit and test intuitions using your new skills rather than discarding them; progress toward a panoramic view of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal training to refine, test, and sometimes restore useful intuitions; aim for an integrated, holistic perspective across fields.
